name: workstation
description: Thin fetch wrapper over the workstation HTTP API: one MCP tool `workstation__tool` taking {tool, params} and POSTing {"tool":..., "params":...} to base_url + tool_path (default http://workstation:8080). No business logic, no SDK, no state.

config_schema.label: Workstation Base URL
config_schema.description: Base URL of the workstation HTTP API (the compose service DNS name http://workstation:8080 inside the omni docker network; the dev overlay publishes host port 12347).

config_schema.label: Tool Path
config_schema.description: Path appended to base_url for a tool invocation; the request is POST {base_url}{tool_path} with body {"tool": <tool>, "params": <params>}.

config_schema.label: HTTP Timeout (s)
config_schema.description: HTTP timeout in seconds for one workstation call (AbortController); a timeout returns a clear isError result, never a hang. 0 = NO timeout (default): the request ends when the workstation answers, the connection fails, or the client cancels it.

config_schema.label: Headers Timeout (s)
config_schema.description: Seconds to wait for the response headers before aborting the HTTP request (the workstation answers only when a worker run finishes, so this must cover the whole run). 0 = disabled (no clock). Default 0 = no timeout at all; positive is an explicit operator opt-in.

config_schema.label: Body Timeout (s)
config_schema.description: Seconds of response-body inactivity before the HTTP request is aborted. 0 = disabled (no clock). Default 0 = no timeout at all; positive is an explicit operator opt-in.

config_schema.label: Authorization Header
config_schema.description: Optional Authorization header value (e.g. "Bearer $secret:WORKSTATION_TOKEN"). Empty = no Authorization header is sent.
